newsitem.title: UK: Refiner demand boosts North Sea tanker rates.
newsitem.headline: Refiner demand boosts North Sea tanker rates.

text.p: North Sea oil tanker freight rates have risen sharply this week amid strong demand from refiners for Aframax tonnage for inter-UK/Cont voyages, Brokers said.

This demand looks likely to be sustained for some time with vessels arleady booked for early November at the current high worldscale numbers, although reduced North Sea crude output for November could trim local requirements later in the month.
"People are already booking for early November at these higher levels," one trader said, "Its purely demand driven".
Worldscale rates for Inter UK/Cont voyages have jumped around 35 points to W140, equivalent to $1 per tonne since last Friday.
Traders said there was no real shortage of tonnage with most of the demand centred on quick-turn-round voyages for Aframax size tonnage in the UK and Hamburg-French Atlantic range.

"The market which has caught the eye all week has been the North Sea where well over 30 fixtures covering all the usual destinations, with 80,000 tonne size finishing the week at W137.5/140 for inter-European movements," Brokers E.A. Gibson said in their weekly report.
Suezmax tonnage achieved W102.5/105 compared with W85 last Friday and a ULCC with 340,000 tonnes was reported traded transatlantic early in the week at W52.5
